key_insight: Foundation ML interatomic potentials can capture simple and some directional low-temperature order in correlated perovskite oxides, but they still fail on purely local spin-state transitions.
engineering_relevance: This sets a clear reliability boundary for using general-purpose MLIPs in screening and simulating complex oxide materials where bond, orbital, and spin ordering affect performance.
method: Tested three foundation MLIPs on LaMnO3 (d4), LaCoO3 (d6), and NdNiO3 (d7) without system-specific training.
Ran 1 ns molecular dynamics on 80- and 160-atom supercells across 50–300 K.
Compared whether each model reproduces three order types: scalar, vector, and on-site spin-order behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports temperature-dependent MD on multiple supercell sizes and shows a hierarchy of outcomes: NdNiO3 is captured, LaMnO3 is partially captured, and LaCoO3 remains inaccessible.
watch_item: General foundation potentials may reproduce energy/geometry trends while still missing symmetry-resolved or local electronic ordering, so they should not be used uncritically for correlated oxides.
paper_title: Bond, orbital and spin order in d4/d6/d7 perovskite oxides: successes and limitations of foundation interatomic potentials
